rics.description: GDP, Current Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, LSEG/National Bureau of Statistics of China
rics.meaning: GDP at Current Prices — nominal GDP level. China's nominal GDP ~CNY 130 trillion (~$18 trillion USD) in 2024 — second-largest economy globally after US.
rics.how_to_use: Use for nominal-GDP arithmetic (debt/GDP, deficit/GDP). Real-vs-nominal gap = GDP deflator — Chinese deflator turned negative 2023-24 (deflation), key macro story.

rics.description: Chg P/P
rics.meaning: China GDP: Chg P/P. Sub-aggregate or alternative measure of GDP.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside headline GDP YoY (aCNCGDPYD/A) for full national accounts picture. Different vintages and aggregations capture different aspects: by-expenditure, by-industry, by-province.

rics.description: Chg Y/Y, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, National Bureau of Statistics of China
rics.meaning: China GDP: Chg Y/Y, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, National Bureau of Statistics of China. Sub-aggregate or alternative measure of GDP.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside headline GDP YoY (aCNCGDPYD/A) for full national accounts picture. Different vintages and aggregations capture different aspects: by-expenditure, by-industry, by-province.

rics.meaning: China GDP: Chg Y/Y, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, National Bureau of Statistics of China. Sub-aggregate or alternative measure of GDP.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside headline GDP YoY (aCNCGDPYD/A) for full national accounts picture. Different vintages and aggregations capture different aspects: by-expenditure, by-industry, by-province.

rics.description: GDP, Growth rate, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: GDP Growth Rate, QoQ (seasonally adjusted) — sequential growth at quarterly frequency.
rics.how_to_use: China only published QoQ-SA from 2011 onwards. Useful for identifying inflection points in real-time. Annualize by ×4 for international comparison.

rics.description: GDP, Growth rate, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: GDP Growth Rate, YoY — alternative release of GDP year-over-year growth (Refinitiv/NBS). Same conceptual measure as aCNCGDPYD/A.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check against the primary release. Use whichever has fresher data; methodology and timing differences across releases are typically minor and resolved on revision.

rics.description: GDP, Growth rate, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: GDP Growth Rate, Year-to-Date YoY — cumulative YTD growth, the official format China publishes for monthly data.
rics.how_to_use: China publishes most data in YTD-cumulative form (a non-Western convention). Convert to single-month/single-quarter by differencing consecutive YTD values. Used in NBS's Monthly Activity Indicators release.

rics.description: GDP per capita, Constant prices, Standardized (based on annual data)
rics.meaning: GDP per capita, constant prices — real income per person. China crossed the World Bank 'high income' threshold in PPP terms but remains in 'upper middle income' at market exchange rates.
rics.how_to_use: China per-capita GDP ~$13,000 (current USD, 2024) — at the threshold of the 'middle-income trap' debate. Sustained 4-5% per-capita real growth needed to reach high-income status by 2035 (CCP target).

rics.description: GDP per capita, Current prices, Standardized (based on annual data)
rics.meaning: China GDP: GDP per capita, Current prices, Standardized (based on annual data). Sub-aggregate or alternative measure of GDP.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside headline GDP YoY (aCNCGDPYD/A) for full national accounts picture. Different vintages and aggregations capture different aspects: by-expenditure, by-industry, by-province.

rics.description: GDP, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, National Bureau of Statistics of China/Refinitiv
rics.meaning: Real GDP Growth, quarter-over-quarter change in constant prices, seasonally adjusted — sequential momentum gauge.
rics.how_to_use: Use for sequential momentum. China QoQ less commonly cited than YoY but useful for identifying turning points. Multiply QoQ by 4 for annualized rate (US-style). Recent QoQ ~1.0-1.5%.

rics.description: GDP, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P, Current Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, National Bureau of Statistics of China/Refinitiv
rics.meaning: China GDP: GDP, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P, Current Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, National Bureau of Statistics of China/Refinitiv. Sub-aggregate or alternative measure of GDP.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside headline GDP YoY (aCNCGDPYD/A) for full national accounts picture. Different vintages and aggregations capture different aspects: by-expenditure, by-industry, by-province.

rics.description: GDP, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, National Bureau of Statistics of China/Refinitiv
rics.meaning: Real GDP Growth, year-over-year change in constant prices — the headline China GDP print. Released quarterly by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) ~3 weeks after quarter-end (e.g., Q1 published ~April 18-20).
rics.how_to_use: THE most-watched China growth number. Annual official target typically 'around 5%'. China hit ~6%+ pre-2018, slowed to 5%-ish post-2020. Sustained sub-4% prints raise hard-landing concerns; >6% would be a re-acceleration story. Markets often question NBS data accuracy — cross-check with industrial production, trade, and the Li Keqiang index (electricity + rail freight + bank loans).

rics.description: GDP, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y, Current Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, National Bureau of Statistics of China/Refinitiv
rics.meaning: Nominal GDP, YoY change in current prices — captures real growth + GDP deflator inflation.
rics.how_to_use: Use for fiscal arithmetic. Recent nominal YoY 4-5% (vs real 5%+) reflects deflator-deflation. Persistent nominal-below-real growth = deflation regime — uniquely concerning for China since 2023.

rics.description: GDP, Standardized, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, National Bureau of Statistics of China/Refinitiv
rics.meaning: GDP at Constant Prices, quarterly (Standardized) — companion to aCNGDPC/C.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check against aCNGDPC/C. Constant-price GDP captures real-output level.

rics.description: GDP, Standardized, Current Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, National Bureau of Statistics of China/Refinitiv
rics.meaning: GDP at Current Prices, quarterly (Standardized) — companion to aCNGDP.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check against aCNGDP. Current-price (nominal) GDP is used in fiscal arithmetic.

rics.description: GDP, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Annual, Refinitiv/National Bureau of Statistics of China
rics.meaning: China GDP: GDP, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Annual, Refinitiv/National Bureau of Statistics of China. Sub-aggregate or alternative measure of GDP.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside headline GDP YoY (aCNCGDPYD/A) for full national accounts picture. Different vintages and aggregations capture different aspects: by-expenditure, by-industry, by-province.

rics.description: GDP, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Quarterly, Refinitiv/National Bureau of Statistics of China
rics.meaning: GDP at Constant Prices, quarterly — real GDP level.
rics.how_to_use: Use for real-level comparisons. NBS publishes constant-price GDP using rolling base years (current 2020 base). YoY growth rate (aCNCGDPYD/A) is the meaningful signal.

rics.description: Exports - Goods & Services, Standardized (based on source annual data)
rics.meaning: Exports of Goods and Services (constant prices) — volume measure of external demand. China is the world's largest goods exporter (~$3.5 trillion annually).
rics.how_to_use: Tracks global goods demand for Chinese manufactures. Sensitive to USD strength (negative for China exports) and US/EU growth. Major Chinese export categories: electronics, machinery, chemicals, autos (rapidly growing — EVs).

rics.description: Imports - Goods & Services, Standardized (based on source annual data)
rics.meaning: Imports of Goods and Services (constant prices) — volume measure of import demand.
rics.how_to_use: Pro-cyclical with industrial activity (raw materials, capital goods) and consumption. Falls during property-led slowdowns. Watch oil + iron ore + soybean imports as the largest sub-categories.

rics.description: Consumer Spending, Standardized (based on source annual data)
rics.meaning: Consumer Spending (Household Final Consumption) — constant-price level. ~38-40% of China GDP — historically low for an economy at China's stage of development; rebalancing toward consumption-led growth is a long-running policy theme.
rics.how_to_use: China's consumption share is ~10-15pp lower than peers — a function of high household savings rate, low wages-to-GDP, and underdeveloped social safety net. Track for 'rebalancing' signal — sustained increases would mark a structural shift away from investment-led growth.

rics.description: Government Consumption, Standardized (based on source annual data)
rics.meaning: Government Consumption — central + local government final consumption (salaries, goods/services). ~16% of GDP.
rics.how_to_use: Track for fiscal-stance signals. Surges signal counter-cyclical fiscal support (e.g., 2020 COVID response). Local-government weakness post-2022 (LGFV stress) is a key macro theme.

rics.description: Gross Fixed Capital Investment, Standardized (based on source annual data)
rics.meaning: Gross Fixed Capital Formation — investment level in real terms. ~42% of GDP, the world's highest investment share for a major economy. Driven by infrastructure (state-led), property, manufacturing capex.
rics.how_to_use: Cycle-sensitive. Property sector ~20% of GFCF historically; deleveraging since 2021 (Three Red Lines) made GFCF a major drag on growth 2022-2024. Watch fixed-asset-investment monthly release (FAI) for higher-frequency signal.
